message:
Hey, a few things for the v4 release.

Can you suggest a codename for the v4 release? We've been naming them after rivers. And rewrite this changelog line to be user-facing: "Refactored auth middleware to fix token refresh race."

Code complete is end of day Thursday 19 November. QA needs two full business days after code complete before anything ships. The release includes a database migration that takes about 90 minutes, and migrations can only run in a maintenance window: Tuesdays 22:00 to 23:00, or Saturdays 02:00 to 04:00. Priya has to be on call for the migration, and she's off from Friday 27 to Sunday 29 November. What's the earliest slot we can run it in?

Also, what's the difference between a feature flag and a config setting, in two sentences? Recommend whether release notes should go out by email or in-app. And give me three things to include in the rollback plan, because last time we didn't have one and it was not fun. Finally, could you draft a short message for the customer-facing status page announcing the maintenance window, once we know the date? A template with a placeholder for the date is fine.
response:
# v4 Release Notes and Planning

## Codename

**Columbia** is my suggestion. Other options are **Mekong**, **Orinoco** or **Shannon**. Check these against the names you've already used.

## Changelog line

> Fixed an issue where some users were unexpectedly signed out or saw authentication errors during longer sessions.

## Earliest migration slot: Saturday 5 December, 02:00–03:30

- **Code complete:** end of day Thursday 19 Nov.
- **QA (two full business days):** Friday 20 and Monday 23 Nov. The release is clear to ship from Tuesday 24 Nov.
- **Tuesday windows don't work.** They're only 60 minutes long and the migration needs about 90, so every Tuesday is out.
- **Saturday 28 Nov doesn't work.** Priya is off from Friday 27 to Sunday 29.
- **Saturday 5 Dec, 02:00–04:00 works.** The 90-minute migration fits with 30 minutes to spare.

If 5 December is too late, your options are to:
- get a 90-minute Tuesday window approved as an exception, which would allow Tuesday 24 Nov, or
- find a backup on-call person for Saturday 28 Nov.

## Feature flag vs. config setting

A feature flag turns a specific feature on or off, usually at runtime and often for chosen users or groups, so you can release it gradually or switch it off quickly. A config setting controls how the system behaves in general (timeouts, endpoints, limits), and it's usually set per environment and rarely changed.

## Email or in-app release notes?

**In-app should be the main channel.** Users see the notes in context, when they're actually using the product, and the notes don't get lost in their inbox. Send a **short email as well** only for changes that affect users, such as the maintenance window, anything that changes how people sign in, or removed features.

## Three things for the rollback plan

1. **A tested database restore or down-migration.** Take a verified backup or snapshot right before the migration, and test the rollback on staging first. Write down how long a restore takes.
2. **Clear go/no-go criteria and a decision deadline.** Decide in advance what triggers a rollback (error rates, failed checks, the migration overrunning) and who makes the call. Set a cut-off time, for example 03:30, after which you roll back instead of trying to fix things in production.
3. **Step-by-step rollback instructions with owners.** List the exact commands or deploy steps to restore the previous app version and schema, who runs each step, and how you'll confirm the rollback worked (smoke tests). Include who notifies customers and the status page.

## Status page template

> **Scheduled Maintenance – [DATE], 02:00–04:00 [TIMEZONE]**
>
> We'll be carrying out scheduled maintenance on [DATE] between 02:00 and 04:00 [TIMEZONE] as part of our v4 release. During this time, [PRODUCT] may be unavailable or experience brief interruptions.
>
> No action is needed on your part. We'll post an update here when maintenance is complete.
>
> Thank you for your patience. If you have questions, contact us at [SUPPORT CONTACT].

If you go with 5 December, the date would be **Saturday 5 December 2026**.
